inspiration.observed_pattern: A per-user visit report applies LEAD over each user's date-ordered events and feeds the next date into DATEDIFF to measure the gap until the next visit.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored member check-in report. Each member's next check-in is found with a two-argument LEAD window, DATEDIFF exposes the day gap, and CASE classifies terminal, same-day, short, and long gaps. The source default-date argument is omitted so terminal rows retain MariaDB's NULL result; the schema, rows, labels, and reporting purpose are new.

fixture_notes: Member 7 has two-day and seven-day gaps; member 8 has a same-day duplicate followed by a three-day gap; member 9 has one terminal check-in and therefore a NULL next-gap. The explicit check-in ID tie-breaker makes same-day window ordering deterministic.
determinism_notes: All member IDs, check-in IDs, and dates are fixed; output and each window use member_id, checkin_date, and checkin_id ordering. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE member_checkins (checkin_id INT PRIMARY KEY, member_id INT NOT NULL, checkin_date DATE NOT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT member_id, checkin_date, DATEDIFF(LEAD(checkin_date) OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY checkin_date, checkin_id), checkin_date) AS days_to_next, CASE WHEN LEAD(checkin_date) OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY checkin_date, checkin_id) IS NULL THEN 'terminal' WHEN DATEDIFF(LEAD(checkin_date) OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY checkin_date, checkin_id), checkin_date) >= 7 THEN 'long-gap' WHEN DATEDIFF(LEAD(checkin_date) OVER (PARTITION BY member_id ORDER BY checkin_date, checkin_id), checkin_date) = 0 THEN 'same-day' ELSE 'short-gap' END AS spacing_class FROM member_checkins ORDER BY member_id, checkin_date, checkin_id
